relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: Solomon's reign claims the whole people.
The kingdom takes shape through named offices close to priesthood and throne.
Writing and memory become instruments of administration.
Military command and priestly authority stand together at the center.
Family networks and friendship bind governance to personal access.
The palace household and forced labor system each receive a manager.
Twelve regions feed the royal household one month at a time.
Ephraim enters the provisioning map.
Cities and valleys are translated into a monthly obligation.
Land becomes an administrative unit for supplying the center.
A regional office is joined to the dynasty through Taphath's marriage.
A wide agricultural and strategic zone is placed beneath one official.
Sixty fortified cities represent both security and concentrated control.
Mahanaim enters the network that once sheltered David.
Naphtali is joined to another marriage involving Solomon's daughter.
Asher's produce and people become part of palace provision.
Issachar is named through its administrator.
Benjamin, once Saul's center, is incorporated into Solomon's system.
Conquered Transjordanian lands are administered beneath the unified throne.
The narrative pictures a numerous people eating, drinking, and rejoicing.
Behind the celebration, neighboring kingdoms pay tribute and serve the imperial center.
Each day consumes vast stores of refined grain.
The royal table absorbs a continuous stream of domesticated and wild animal life.
Dominion and surrounding peace are narrated from the throne's perspective.
The deepest image of peace is modest: each household secure beneath vine and fig tree.
Thousands of horses and chariots reveal the military infrastructure beneath that peace.
Regional officers ensure that the royal table never experiences lack.
Even animal feed travels through assigned systems of extraction and delivery.
Solomon receives a heart wide enough to hold complexity.
The court measures his wisdom against renowned neighboring traditions.
Named sages remind us that wisdom existed beyond Solomon even as the text elevates him.
Proverbs and songs pour from the royal imagination.
Wisdom attends to cedar, wall-growing herb, animal, bird, crawler, and fish.
The world comes to hear, while the question remains whether royal wisdom will listen back.

contemplative_note: A wise administration can still become an extraction machine. The test of the broad heart is whether the vine-and-fig-tree peace reaches those who grow the food, pay the tribute, carry the loads, serve the palace, and live beyond imperial borders.
